{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"d647465574b69ee0a6e5c338099e62445afb38117f34e67a131650921a21efb4","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"License laws, license types and identity verification","heading":"C — License laws, license types, the license issuance process and ID verification (Standard and REAL ID)","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — License laws, license types, the license issuance process and ID verification (Standard and REAL ID)
Knowledge domain: the basic laws every New Jersey motorist must follow about carrying and updating a license, the license types and ages, how cards are issued, and how Standard and REAL ID applicants prove identity, address and Social Security number.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Anyone driving in New Jersey must carry a valid license, a valid probationary license, or a validated New Jersey permit, and must also carry valid insurance and registration cards. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
A driver using a validated New Jersey permit must always have an appropriately licensed driver along. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
After moving, a motorist has one week to report the new address to the MVC, and this rule also covers people moving out of the state. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
A legal name change, such as through marriage, divorce or a court order, must be reported to the MVC within two weeks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
A new resident holding a valid out-of-state license must apply for a New Jersey license within 60 days, or before the old license expires if that is sooner. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
The newcomer deadline for a commercial driver license (CDL) is 30 days, and the out-of-state license is surrendered once the New Jersey license is received. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
A motorist whose valid license comes from another country may drive on it for up to one year. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
Commercial vehicle drivers face tougher testing than car or motorcycle drivers and must already hold a valid basic New Jersey license before they apply for a CDL. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
Anyone who has never held a driver license must complete the Graduated Driver License (GDL) Program, which phases in privileges after a stretch of supervised driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
A license applicant under 18 must present a consent form that a parent or guardian has completed and signed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
A Standard license applicant provides proof of a Social Security or Taxpayer Identification Number (or an affidavit of ineligibility), 1 proof of New Jersey address and 6 points of identification. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
A REAL ID license applicant provides 2 proofs of New Jersey address, 1 proof of the full Social Security number and 6 points of identification, including proof of lawful presence in the United States. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
Identification documents must be written in English or be accompanied by an approved translation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
Drivers under 21 holding an examination permit, special learner's permit or probationary license must show two reflective GDL decals, supplied by the MVC, on the vehicle's license plates. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
When the manual and a statute or regulation disagree, the statute or regulation is what governs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A03
An endorsement expires together with the license it is on, except Hazmat, which requires retesting every 2 years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A03
When an endorsement is added to an existing license, its charge is prorated for the time left until the license expires. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A03
Since a 2021 security upgrade, every New Jersey license and non-driver ID, Standard or REAL ID, is produced at a secure central facility that uses facial recognition to fight identity theft. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A03
At the transaction you receive a temporary license or ID that is valid for 30 days, and the card itself is mailed to you, with delivery expected within 30 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A03
Motorists under 21 receive a vertical-format license or non-driver ID card, and licenses and IDs are valid for four years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A03
Altering a license or ID, obtaining one by fraud, or presenting an altered one can bring loss of driving privileges, fines up to $1,000, imprisonment, or a combination. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A04
The basic automobile license covers every MVC-registered Class D vehicle except motorcycles, with a minimum age of 18 and a permit age of 16. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A04
The basic automobile license chart lists a $10 permit fee and license fees of $24 Standard or $35 REAL ID, and requires knowledge, vision and road tests. [A04]
Why it matters: dynamic detail: the manual says fees are subject to change.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A04
The probationary automobile license has a minimum age of 17 with a permit at 16, a permit fee of $10 plus $4 for red reflectorized decals, and a $63 license fee. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A04
A commercial driver license covers large trucks, buses and similar vehicles in Classes A, B and C, carries a $125 permit fee and adds a commercial test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A04
A motorcycle license (Class E) covers most vehicles with fewer than four wheels and is issued either as its own license or as an M endorsement on a basic New Jersey license, with a minimum age of 17. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A05
A moped license is for unlicensed motorists aged 15 or older and is not required for anyone who holds a Class A, B, C, D or E license. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A05
An agricultural license is only for farming, may be granted to people aged 16 to 17, and lasts four years or until the holder gets a basic license at 18. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A05
A boat license is for people 16 or older running a motorboat on fresh, non-tidal waters, and every power-vessel operator must show a Boating Safety Certificate when applying. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A05
In the license chart, K means the Knowledge test, V the Vision test, R the Road test and C the Commercial test. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A05
CDL applicants must be at least 18, and those under 21 may drive only inside New Jersey and cannot receive HAZMAT or passenger endorsements. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A06
A Standard license applicant needs a mix of documents: one or more primary documents, one or more secondary documents, a total of at least six ID points, and proof of a New Jersey home address. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A06
A REAL ID applicant must prove age, identity, Social Security number and lawful presence using the 2+1+6 combination, with at least one primary and one secondary document among them. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A06
If your current legal name differs from your birth certificate, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a certified marriage or civil union certificate, divorce decree, or court order linking the names. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A06
A divorce decree supports going back to a previous name only if it lists both the married and previous names and permits the return to the previous name. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A06
Identity documents must be unlaminated originals or certified copies, in English, and carry the required state or municipal seal. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A06
If documents conflict the MVC may ask for more, and it may refuse any permit or license application when a document looks altered, false or invalid. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A07
Primary proofs of identity for a Standard license include a US birth certificate, a US passport or passport card, a passport from the applicant's country of citizenship, and a digitized New Jersey license or non-driver ID. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A07
A foreign-issued photo driver license counts toward identity only when it is presented together with another government-issued document. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A07
A Standard license proof of New Jersey residency must show the applicant's name and home address, for example a utility or credit card bill up to one year old or a pay stub up to six months old. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A08
For a Standard license, no primary or secondary document may be more than three years past its expiration date. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F42 | anchor: A08
Standard license applicants may count no more than two 1-point documents toward their six points. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

Misconceptions: a validated permit does not let you drive alone; the address-change deadline applies even if you are leaving the state; a temporary paper license is not the finished card, which arrives by mail; a foreign photo license cannot stand alone as identity proof.
Mnemonics: REAL ID is two plus one plus six (two address proofs, one full Social Security proof, six points); a move is reported in one week and a name change in two weeks — Move fast, Name next.
Glossary: GDL means the Graduated Driver License Program for new drivers; REAL ID means the federally compliant license version proven with the two-plus-one-plus-six model; endorsement means an added privilege on a license, such as M for motorcycle; primary and secondary documents are the two tiers of identity proof that add up to the six points.
Dynamic facts: license and permit fees, phone numbers, website addresses and online document selectors can change; the manual itself says fees are subject to change, so confirm current values on the MVC website.
